# Best portable power station for a CPAP

For most people, a roughly 1,000 Wh LiFePO4 unit with pure sine wave output and a fast UPS switchover is the right size. It covers about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and 1.2-1.7 nights with it on.

## My picks

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,024 Wh)**
- Tested Watts picks it as best overall: about 20 dB rated noise, 10 ms UPS switchover, and a ~49 min wall recharge. They estimate about 1.7 humidified nights. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)
- BuyerSheet lists it at about $700. [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)
- The search results didn't include a direct purchase link for it, so use the "Check official store" links on the BuyerSheet page.

**Best if you want expandability: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (1,024 Wh, expandable to 5 kWh)**
- It's under 10 ms UPS and under 30 dB, and weighs 27.6 lb. Expanded, it could cover roughly 8 humidified nights. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)
- It's about $719. [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

**Best value with a buy link: BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W)**
- It's rated about 3.1 nights humidifier off and 1.4 nights on. [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)
- It's $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF, which was tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. [Buy the AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (Dealectric earns a commission, at no cost to you.) [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/)
- The sources don't give an AC180 UPS switchover time, so check Bluetti's spec page if you want it to take over automatically during an outage while you sleep. BuyerSheet lists it at 35.3 lb, while PowerStationTips says 16.5 lb, so confirm the weight before buying.

**Small and light, one night only: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (286 Wh, 10.4 lb)**
- It's under 10 ms UPS and about $299. It covers roughly one night humidifier off (estimates run 0.5-0.8 nights), and it doesn't cover a humidified night unless you add a battery. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)

## Things to check
- **Pure sine wave** output is the baseline requirement. [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)
- **The humidifier roughly doubles power draw.** Sites assume different nightly use (520 Wh vs. 720 Wh with humidifier), so measure your own machine with a watt meter if you can.
- **Using your CPAP's DC cord** on the 12 V port skips inverter losses and adds about 10-20% runtime. Use only the CPAP maker's approved cord.
- **Jackery's Explorer 1000 v2** is a good travel unit, but Jackery says its power stations aren't recommended for medical or life-support devices, and its UPS is up to 20 ms. I'd skip it for CPAP unless your CPAP maker confirms it's fine. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)
- **Flying:** none of these can go on a plane. For air travel you need a battery under about 100 Wh.

This is general information, not medical advice. If you depend on your CPAP, ask your provider or equipment supplier about a backup plan.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and how many nights you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
